description: `nonNull(value)` is the same test as `!isNull(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Strictly `null`. `undefined` is a separate case — `isNil` covers both.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not `null`; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonNull(undefined); // => true
nonNull(0); // => true
nonNull(""); // => true
nonNull(null); // => false
```
